title: Make LLM Inference Affordable to Everyone: Augmenting GPU Memory with NDP-DIMM
problem: Deploying large LLMs (e.g., LLaMA2-70B) on consumer-grade GPUs with limited VRAM is impractical; offloading model weights to host DRAM or NVMe storage creates severe bandwidth bottlenecks on the PCIe interconnect, resulting in very low inference throughput.
motivation: As LLM-assisted services proliferate, democratizing LLM inference on budget consumer hardware (rather than expensive server-grade HBM-equipped GPUs) is a pressing need.
method: The system recognizes that LLM neurons (the basic units) aren't equally important—some get used much more than others depending on the input. It keeps the frequently-used 20% of neurons that handle 80% of the work on the consumer GPU for speed, and offloads the rarely-used 80% of neurons that only handle 20% of work to processing units embedded in DRAM chips, so computation happens right at the data instead of moving weights across the slow PCIe link. A lightweight predictor watches each input to identify which neurons will be active, and a scheduler balances work across multiple DRAM modules while the GPU and DRAM chips compute in parallel.
key_novelty: It recognizes that LLMs use some weights much more than others, and stores the rarely-used weights in processing units built into DRAM chips rather than shuttling all weights across the slow PCIe connection, so computation happens right where the data lives.
contributions: Hot/cold neuron classification leveraging ~80/20 activation sparsity split in LLMs
Heterogeneous GPU + NDP-DIMM execution strategy with a lightweight real-time neuron predictor
Window-based online load-balancing scheduler across NDP-DIMM modules
75.24x average speedup over state-of-the-art offloading inference systems; LLaMA2-70B at 13.75 tokens/s on consumer hardware

metrics.speedup: 75.24x average over state-of-the-art offloading-based inference on consumer hardware

limitations: The hot/cold neuron split assumes significant activation sparsity, which may not hold uniformly across all LLM architectures and input distributions.
primary_theme: near-DRAM processing for affordable LLM inference
